answer: A dispute-bonded escrow stops fakes draining the nectar payout. Before a voyage, each agent locks 40 units and publishes route evidence. A gale audit re-checks; peers dispute suspects with an equal bond. Verifiers re-run one sample; copied evidence slashes the cluster. The k-th fake costs 40k units, risking its own 40 plus 40(k-1) from siblings, growing with n; slashed escrow cannot be reused, and failure loses all escrow. One fake costs 40; 1,000 risk 20,020,000. A device farm fails on matching fingerprints. An honest agent locks 40 once and keeps the nectar reward.
